Triangular coordinate reduction is proved by induction on the number of processed coordinates in an actual arbitrary group. Right multiplication by an actual lattice member with negative integer floor changes the pivot coordinate by that integer, preserves earlier coordinates, and updates the lattice factor so g=x*gamma remains exact. No commutativity, bounded representative, quotient compactness or normal lattice hypothesis replaces this argument. Empty coordinate types are covered.

A finite linear order is enumerated by an actual order isomorphism from Fin. Reduction then produces coordinates in [0,1). A genuine coordinate homeomorphism maps the compact closed unit cube into an actual compact set of representatives. The original natural group coset space is proved compact from its actual projection, including nonnormal lattices.

Unitriangular is the actual subgroup of matrix units having upper-triangular values and diagonal one. Product and inverse closure are proved with actual matrix multiplication and inversion. Every such matrix has determinant one and defines a genuine matrix unit. Its inverse is its actual adjugate.

Off-diagonal coordinates use descending row and ascending column order. A coordinate matrix is constructed for every finite coordinate tuple and proved inverse to the actual entry chart. Both maps are continuous in the inherited matrix-unit topology; inverse-chart continuity uses the polynomial adjugate. Explicit matrix annotations prevent accidental selection of the pointwise function-space monoid.

The original integer lattice is the range of the actual group homomorphism from integral unitriangular matrix units to real ones induced by the integer cast ring homomorphism. Membership is characterized exactly by integral off-diagonal entries. Its discreteness follows from an open half-unit coordinate neighborhood isolating the identity, and its closedness follows in the actual Hausdorff topological group.

Actual integral right transvections are in that original lattice. Matrix multiplication proves the pivot and earlier-coordinate laws: only one column changes, and entries below the pivot row vanish. Applying the proved reduction establishes bounded representatives and compactness for the actual real group quotient without a supplied cocompactness hypothesis.

Actual depth-k subgroups impose zero entries for positive column-row gaps below k. Product closure follows coefficientwise. Inverse closure is proved directly from the actual u*inverse(u)=1 matrix equation, using upper-triangular inverse support and diagonal one. The subgroups decrease with depth and are trivial at depth at least n; no lower-central or commutator-law identification is assumed.

Each actual depth subgroup has a constructed global coordinate homeomorphism using its allowed entries, with forbidden entries set to zero. Its closedness follows from the actual coefficient zero sets. Local compactness and second countability follow from these finite real coordinate charts.

The restricted depth lattice is exactly the comap of the original integer lattice under the actual subgroup inclusion. Its integer right-transvection coordinate laws are proved, giving actual bounded representatives and compact natural coset quotients for every n and k. Its discreteness follows from the topological embedding into the original integer lattice; closedness follows from the original lattice closedness. These are conclusions, not compactness inputs.

The inclusion-induced map of restricted group cosets is constructed as an actual quotient lift. Its representative formula, continuity, injectivity and exact projected subgroup image are proved with the original nonnormal-lattice equivalence relation. Compact restricted quotient plus Hausdorff ambient quotient proves a closed embedding. This is instantiated for every concrete depth subgroup, with compact projected orbits and metrizable natural quotients.

The fixed paper Section 07 lines 13-22 requires rational subgroup/lattice facts for arbitrary connected simply connected nilpotent Lie groups; lines 23-32 require a strong commutator filtration; lines 47-95 use these for cube compactness. This round establishes actual noncommutative lattice and layer-quotient geometry in arbitrary-dimensional unitriangular models. It does not prove the general rational subgroup theorem, matrix depth commutator law or nilpotency-class bound, group/Lie lower-central comparison, exponential/BCH/Malcev correspondence, or identification of the original paper models and their specified lattices with these models.
